analysis: Examined two additive changes. (1) ProcessMemoryLedger.swift head lines 204-224 add capacityShortfall(growthBytes:additionalSystemReserveBytes:). It is read-only: it takes the ledger lock, calls prepareUsageReader() before the lock (consistent with the documented lock order and the allocator-init-outside-lock rule), and reads usage once under the lock. Overflow is handled by try? with saturation to .max, and Self.subtract floors at zero. The unmaterialized term (charged - materialized) cannot underflow, since install and recordMaterialization maintain materialized <= charged. It mutates no charge, owner or policy state, so admission via replaceCharge/recheckCharge is unchanged. The result is a diagnostic reclaim-shortfall value. A caller that trusts this value to decide eviction or reclaim could misbehave, but no such caller is in the supplied evidence. (2) WholeMacServiceBudget.swift head lines 231-251 add isIdle(for:), performIfIdle(for:_:), and isIdleLocked. performIfIdle runs a closure under the budget lock, which blocks acquire and beginUnboundedActivity during the closure. The documented contract is that the body must not reenter the budget. The lock is a non-recursive NSLock, so reentry would deadlock; this is an availability hazard for future callers, not an exploitable issue here. Idle is judged by charges.isEmpty, unboundedActivities.isEmpty, and the clock; it is consistent with the existing quiescenceSatisfiedLocked. No new caller, I/O, or crypto is visible. Relevant threat IDs, if any caller later uses this for cache or KV maintenance, are T-028, T-029, and T-041 (TB-007). Remaining integration questions: which callers use performIfIdle and whether their bodies are short and non-blocking, and whether the shortfall value feeds any reclaim or eviction path that could affect cached KV or T-041 behavior. Neither is in the supplied evidence, so no finding is raised.
